description.summary: the input devices the compositor manages

protocol.description:
A read-only list of the input devices the compositor manages, with what each one can be configured to do, for MATE's input preferences, which cannot see devices on Wayland. Device settings stay where MATE keeps them (GSettings); the compositor applies them. This protocol only describes the devices.
It identifies the user's hardware, so a compositor should offer the global only to trusted MATE components, and never to clients in a sandbox.
Versioning. This protocol follows the usual Wayland rules: a later version only adds requests, events and enum values, and a client must ignore enum and bitfield values it does not know.

interface.name: mate_input_device_manager_v1
interface.description: After binding, the compositor sends a device event for every device, then done. Later it sends device for each new device, followed by done, and removed on the device object when one goes.

event.name: device
event.description: Its properties follow on the new object, ending with its own done.

event.name: done
event.description: Sent after the initial devices, and after each batch of new ones.

request.name: stop
request.description: The compositor sends finished and no further events on this object. Device objects stay valid.

event.name: finished

description.summary: the compositor sends no more events

event.description: After this event the client should destroy the object.

interface.name: mate_input_device_v1
interface.description: Every event below except removed belongs to a group that ends with done. The full state is sent after creation; later, only what changed is sent, followed by done.

enum.name: config
enum.description: As libinput reports them for the device.

entry.name: dwtp
entry.summary: disable while using the pointing stick

entry.name: scroll_button
entry.summary: scrolling while a button is held

entry.name: disabled
entry.summary: the device can be turned off

entry.name: disabled_on_external_mouse
entry.summary: the device can turn off while a mouse is plugged in

event.name: id

description.summary: a stable id for the device

event.description: At most 255 bytes of ASCII letters, digits and "_", ".", "-", ":" and "@". The same device gets the same id across reconnections and sessions. Clients that keep per-device settings store them under it and treat it as opaque.

event.name: kind
event.description: How preferences should list it. A touchpad is a pointer with tap fingers or a touchpad udev tag; a pointing stick and a trackball are told apart from a mouse by their udev tags.

description.summary: the kinds of events the device sends

event.name: buttons

description.summary: the pointer buttons the device has

event.description: A clickpad has a left button (pressing it clicks); a touchpad that can only tap has none.

description.summary: the number of fingers that can tap
the acceleration profiles the device supports
the scroll methods the device supports
the click methods the device supports
the ways the device can be turned off

event.name: output

description.summary: the monitor the device is mapped to

event.description: For a touchscreen or tablet, the mate_output_v1 id of the monitor it is mapped to (see mate-output-v1); empty when it is not mapped or is not such a device.

description.summary: end of a group of changes

event.name: removed
event.description: The object then sends no more events, and the client should destroy it.
